description:
Demand derivation discovers its inputs one per run: each run finds one more
missing fact, waits on it, and re-runs when it arrives, instead of
registering every wait it can know in one run.

Reduced case: `def main(), do: Enum.take([1, 2, 3], 2)`.
Measured: DeriveInputDemand 127 runs / 36 subjects; Enum.take/2 alone 16
runs, woken by EntryDispatch of Enum.count/1, count/2, count_result/2,
drop_positive/2, reduce/3, ... one at a time (52 such wakes), plus
StaticCallees (34). DeriveRuntimeDemand 158 / 40, woken by ExecutableFacts
settled (40) and RuntimeDemandInputs (74, 35 of them coalesced).
Paper: a job knows its full read set from facts it already holds (the
static callees, then their entry dispatches), so it waits on all of them at
once and runs again only when all are satisfied (the scheduler already
re-runs a waiter only when ALL its waits are satisfied). Predicted:
DeriveInputDemand runs <= 2 per subject (discover, compute), unless a
genuinely new callee appears.

Settle with a reader first: whether the serial shape is the job returning
after its first missing read, or waits being discovered through facts that
only exist after the previous wait resolves (a true chain). A true chain is
legitimate; the paper must say which links are.

Acceptance: measured runs per subject match the paper for both kinds on the
reduced case; no pin rises.

## Learned from the smallest case (2026-09-25)

Case: `def main(), do: 1` (44 runs, 26 subjects = 13 kinds x {main/0,
def/1 macro root}). Ledger: scratchpad wave2/r_s1_ledger/ledger.md.
The def/1 chain is accepted by design (the owner: the cost of def as a
real macro).

1. The smallest shape of this disease is inside one function, not across
   callees. DeriveInputDemand runs 3 times per subject on s1 for both main/0
   and def/1: the walk `collect_input_forwarding_graph` waits on
   StaticCallees(f) and returns (keying.rs:385-389); the next run waits on
   EntryDispatch(f) and returns (keying.rs:407-412); the third computes.
   OBSERVED: PlanEntryDispatch(0) concludes from FunctionDefined(0) alone,
   never reading StaticCallees (dispatch.rs:104-191; trace span 40).
   OPEN, needs a probe before the paper: the order is deliberate per
   keying.rs:382-384 -- StaticCallees' producer settles the
   provider-boundary question, and a provider boundary (or a function with
   no LoweredBody) skips EntryDispatch entirely. Asking for both at once is
   only safe if EntryDispatch always has a producer that concludes for such
   a function; otherwise the AND-wait blocks forever. The probe: does
   PlanEntryDispatch conclude for an extern / provider-boundary function?

2. Relation to fz-afu.2 (gated job starts): both rungs are nameable from
   the subject plus facts present, so once afu.2 lands they are gates and
   the job is not started until they hold (afu.2 predicts DeriveInputDemand
   6 -> 2 on s1). What remains for this ticket is the walk into callees:
   each callee's rungs become nameable only after the caller's EntryDispatch
   and forwards are read. INFERRED: that walk is itself the gate
   declaration evaluated over facts present, so this ticket may reduce to
   "a gate declaration may walk the forwarding graph" -- re-measure the
   Enum.take numbers on top of afu.2 before writing the paper.

3. Not this disease: the two ScopeCode(source_owner=17) repeats on s1 are
   a true chain. The first waits on FunctionDefined(def/1): the name `def`
   resolves to a FunctionId only through the namespace ScopeCode(16) built,
   which ScopeCode(17) consults during its walk (IndexCode(17) sees only an
   unresolved ScopeForm::MacroCall, source_publish.rs:346-361). The second
   waits on RootBackendProduct(root=1), whose RootId is minted from
   FunctionDefined(1)'s payload (world.rs:1045-1060) -- it cannot be named
   before that fact exists. Both links are legitimate; they stay.
title: Demand derivation discovers its waits one per run
